I agree these are different. I think it makes sense to separate these out. Is there a better name than backends? I could live with backends but that didn't immediately make it clear this is code to support some of our meson options.
What should they be called instead of backends?

Can you talk more about your overall vision here?

Where the line is for
src/ 
include/ 
backends/ 
is still a little blurry to me. 

E.g.

http/
redfish-core/

E.g. 
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/include/async_resp.hpp I would think would fit better in http/

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/include/sessions.hpp is in include/ but then there are similar redfish utils at https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/tree/master/redfish-core/include/utils

There are still some "Redfish" hits in http/
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fbmcweb+redfish+NOT+path%3A%2F%5Eredfish-core%5C%2F%2F+NOT+path%3A%2F%5Etest%5C%2F%2F+path%3A%2F%5Ehttp%5C%2F%2F&type=code

A more traditional C++ project of high-level dirs of src/ include/ lib/ is what I would lean towards. E.g. redfish-core/, http/ backends/ are not at the root. 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2360734/whats-a-good-directory-structure-for-larger-c-projects-using-makefile

That said, I don't care as long as our future vision makes sense to developers.

> Can you talk more about your overall vision here?
> 
> Where the line is for
> src/ 
> include/ 
> backends/ 
> is still a little blurry to me. 


backends -> Individual handlers for a specific purpose, organized in folders by ownership.
include/src (should be combined) -> Generic code that doesn't really belong anywhere else.
backends/redfish-core -> Code specific to redfish
http -> Code related to HTTP parsing/orchestration/routing


The big part is that I want to have a separation such that:
A. when people fork the code, they're adding their own "backend" folder, and thus isolating their code from others.  That way, if/when it gets upstreamed, it has fewer merge conflicts
B. Different routes are separate by folders.  At some point, it seems very likely that we split redfish-core into redfish-core and redfish-dbus, given that there are those are are using bmcweb to build their own custom non-openbmc implementations.  I want to be able to support that open source effort without imposing a lot of overhead on openbmc or the submitters.  Separating the code on a backend boundary seems like a start to that.
C. We can decide which code needs to "die" or is unmaintained.  For example, I think the dbus-rest stuff is dead, but I don't really want to delete the code entirely because I suspect there's people still using it.  Separating it out into a folder means we can remove it from the majority of the CI/build (and subsequently take back the compile time improvements) and if folks want to continue to compile/maintain it, they can propose themselves as reviewers/maintainers and turn it back on.

> 
> E.g. 
> Why move some of the webui code here, but not all of it like https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/include/webassets.hpp ?

webassets isn't specific to the UI, so I was somewhat treating it like "generic" code, although I could certainly see the argument it should be a "backend".  It also has some weirdness where the http layer interacts with it for maintaining the allowlist, so it's non-trivial to move in this commit.

> 
> 
> Even the lines for 
> http/
> redfish-core/ 
> Can get a little blurry

Maybe I've looked at this too long, but the way I see it:
http -> is this a generic HTTP/RFC concept?
redfish-core -> Is this a Redfish concept?

The only big piece of overlap today is privileges, and in the future at some point I'd like to fix that.

> 
> E.g. 
> https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/include/async_resp.hpp I would think would fit better in http/

Agreed, but it's not a backend, so I didn't really move it in this commit which is focusing on breaking out backends.  Honestly, I think the whole AsyncResp class could go away and just be merged with Response, but that's a problem for another day.

> 
> https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/include/sessions.hpp is in include/ but then there are similar redfish utils at https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/tree/master/redfish-core/include/utils

That's exactly what I'm starting to clean up with https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/65720

but again, unrelated to breaking out backends.
